criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines name the asserter (Gov. Dunleavy), the dollar figure ($150M), the scale (one-gigawatt), and signal correction without snark. ~183 chars, within the ~210-char LinkedIn cutoff. 'The cooling math is real' is a mild warm-up that slightly delays the tension.

criteria.name: Claim load-bearing + AK stakes
criteria.notes: The $150M cooling figure is the quantified anchor of the state's hyperscaler pitch and is cited in the SB 250 incentive debate and JBER/Eielson/Clear land-lease terms. Correction names concrete dollar-tied AK consequence: incentive packages and allocator siting models sized against the wrong variable.

criteria.name: Steelman fairness
criteria.notes: Para three delivers a generous, physics-grounded steelman citing Nordic precedent (Lulea, Iceland) and 'real money at gigawatt scale.' No snark; the believer feels fairly represented. Stops at the physics layer rather than engaging the strongest magnitude defense.

criteria.name: Counter-evidence quality
criteria.notes: Four counter-items traceable to dossier: UAF ACEP Feb 2024 (primary), ACEP Mar 2025 (primary), ADN rate analysis (credible secondary), Chugach/GVEA gas statements (primary). The GVEA bullet lacks inline source attribution and the ADN rate figures are secondary aggregation.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics at near-every-sentence density: Dunleavy, one-gigawatt, $150M, UAF ACEP, Feb 2024, 5 percent, Chugach, 14-17c/kWh, Virginia 8.99c, Texas 6.12c, ACEP Mar 2025, SB 250, JBER, Eielson, Clear, GVEA, Cook Inlet, 30 percent to under 1 percent.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Attribution traces to two dossier asserter entries (Data Center Knowledge, Broadband Breakfast). Counter rests on two primary UAF ACEP findings and a primary utility statement; the rate comparison is sourced to an ADN op-ed rather than EIA/tariff data. All in dossier.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Closely matches post_001.md: analytical, structural, business-literate ('not the one a CFO is solving for'), corrective without contempt. No influencer cadence, hype, or banned phrases. 'The more accurate frame, in short' nudges slightly editorial.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Tight 2-4 sentence paragraphs, one bullet block of 4 single-clause items, ~446 words within 350-475, total chars well under 3000. Easy to scan on desktop and mobile.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Specific, debatable, tied to the corrected frame (power price as dominant variable), no softeners or CTA. The two-part structure slightly diffuses the single sharpest debate tension.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: A CFO/program manager/allocator can name a decision to reframe: whether SB 250 sizing or JBER/Eielson lease modeling should anchor on the $150M cooling figure or on Alaska's worst-in-nation power rate. No rough breakeven number offered.

one_sentence_fix: Add an inline source attribution for the GVEA Cook Inlet gas figure and, where possible, replace the ADN electricity-rate aggregation with a direct EIA or Chugach tariff citation to lift every rebuttal point to primary-source level.
